assumptions: CSV row order is the temporal order because labels 2026-02-29 through 2026-02-48 are not valid ISO calendar dates.
The prediction task is one-step-ahead/current-row target estimation after the preceding row target and current feature are available.
Training-only median imputation is admissible for missing feature values; no interpolation across future rows is used.
MAE is the predefined selection metric and RMSE is a secondary diagnostic; the two validation-fold MAEs receive equal weight.
The field note stating that feature is available at prediction time is accepted as local case evidence.

baseline.description: Naive persistence: predict row t target as the observed target from row t-1; it has no fitted parameters.
evidence: Minimal executable sanity check verified that the row-2 persistence prediction is 51.676, exactly row 1 target.
baseline.result: Validation fold MAE 0.966375 and 2.183500 (mean 1.5749375); untouched rows 41-48 test MAE 0.814375 and RMSE 1.0976922952 (n=8).

candidate_models: OLS regression on current feature, previous target, and ordinal row: low implementation and fit cost, training-median imputation, but sensitive to shift and saturation/leverage. It was rejected because mean validation MAE 5.635087 exceeded persistence 1.5749375; fold-2 MAE was 10.412884. Falsified as preferred if its repeated temporal MAE does not beat persistence.

Winsorized Huber IRLS regression on current feature, previous target, and ordinal row: moderate implementation cost; feature is clipped to training 5th/95th percentiles and residuals use Huber weights. It improves fold-1 MAE to 0.683021 but was rejected because mean validation MAE 4.631156 and fold-2 MAE 8.579292 exceeded persistence. Falsified as preferred by failure under the observed regime transition.

Naive persistence: structurally distinct parameter-free time-series baseline, negligible implementation/fit cost, assumes local continuity. It was selected by the predefined lowest mean validation MAE rule. It would be falsified by repeated forward folds showing a candidate reliably lower MAE or by operations requiring forecasts before the prior target is observed.
claims: Verified evidence supports provisional selection of persistence under the predefined validation MAE rule.
Verified held-out test MAE is 0.814375 for persistence on rows 41-48; this is descriptive evidence for this synthetic sample, not a deployment guarantee.
Verified leakage fields were perfectly aligned with current or next targets and were excluded before modeling.
No claim is marked FINAL; operational fitness, causal validity, and generalization beyond the 48 local rows are not claimed.

data_findings: Verified 48 rows and seven CSV columns.
Verified target_proxy equals target in all 48 rows.
Verified future_target equals the following row target for all 47 comparable row pairs.
Excluded future_target, target_proxy, and regime from every fitted model; retained noise_feature only as a named negative control and did not fit on it.
Verified missing feature values at rows 9 and 31 and feature=180 at row 40.
Verified 20 invalid calendar labels, 2026-02-29 through 2026-02-48; experiment therefore uses explicit ordinal row boundaries.
experiment_design: Predeclared primary metric MAE, secondary metric RMSE, and selection by lowest unweighted mean MAE across two forward validation folds.
Fold 1 trains rows 1-24 and validates 25-32; fold 2 expands training to rows 1-32 and validates 33-40, explicitly testing the late transition and sensor saturation interval.
After selection, train/final history is rows 1-40 and the sole test window is rows 41-48; persistence needs no fitting but candidates are refit on this history.
All candidate features are current feature, prior target, and ordinal time; OLS and winsorized Huber use only training-derived imputation/scaling/clipping.
Randomness is confined to bootstrap resampling and feature jitter, both controlled by seed 20260901; model fitting itself is deterministic.
falsification_tests: Observed fold-2 transition falsified the proposition that either fitted regression is preferable under the predefined mean-MAE rule: OLS and winsorized Huber fold-2 MAEs were 10.412884 and 8.579292 versus persistence 2.183500.

The first executable run falsified the initial implementation's implicit assumption that every training row has a prior target; row 1 caused KeyError. The fit was corrected to exclude row 1 while retaining row 1 as history for row 2.

A future repeated forward evaluation with candidate mean MAE below persistence, preferably with an uncertainty interval excluding zero for paired loss differences, would falsify the present provisional selection.
If prediction must occur before y_(t-1) is available, persistence feasibility is falsified and the task must be reopened at the availability/formalization subtask.

constraints: All splits preserve order and training rows precede evaluation rows.
No future_target, target_proxy, or regime predictor is permitted.
Preprocessing statistics are fitted on each training window only.
Test rows 41-48 are not used in model selection.
notes: Subtask trace: audit consumes CSV plus field notes and emits availability/leakage decisions; split design consumes row order and emits fixed ordinal windows; fitting consumes allowed predictors and training rows and emits predictions; evaluation consumes predictions/targets and emits MAE/RMSE; robustness consumes the selected rule, fixed seed, and perturbations and emits sensitivity evidence.

Controllable decisions were model family, allowed predictors, split boundaries, imputation, robust clipping, metrics, and seed; target values, field-note availability, row order, missingness, saturation, and small sample size were treated as non-controllable constraints.

Decision record: initial candidates were appended before execution; selection superseded candidate preference with persistence after both forward validation folds. Rejected candidate results and the first failed execution remain recorded.
formalization.objective: Select the feasible model minimizing unweighted mean validation MAE; report test MAE and RMSE only after selection.
parameters: Validation folds: train rows 1-24/evaluate 25-32 and train rows 1-32/evaluate 33-40.
Final fit rows 1-40 and untouched test rows 41-48.
Huber cutoff 1.345 robust scale units, at most 50 IRLS iterations, and training feature clipping at empirical 0.05/0.95 quantiles.
Paired test bootstrap uses 2000 resamples with seed 20260901.
units: target, feature, MAE, and RMSE use the unspecified numeric units of the local CSV.
time is an ordinal row index because the supplied calendar-like labels become invalid after 2026-02-28.
variables: y_t: target at ordinal row t.
x_t: feature available at prediction time, with training-only median imputation when missing.
hat_y_t: one-step prediction; persistence sets hat_y_t=y_(t-1).

human_gates: No human approval was requested or received.
Before any operational use, a domain owner must confirm forecast timing, availability of y_(t-1), units, loss function, acceptable thresholds, and handling of invalid time labels.
Additional post-transition data and a locked evaluation protocol are required before reconsidering a FINAL model decision.
reality_constraints: future_target is created after outcomes and is unavailable at prediction time.
regime is known only after period close and is unavailable at prediction time.
target_proxy is a direct export of the current target and cannot be a predictor.
feature has missing observations at rows 9 and 31 and a documented sensor-saturation value 180 at row 40.
Only 48 ordered observations exist; the late regime begins at row 33, leaving little independent post-shift evidence.
No user or domain-owner approval was provided, so model choice is experimental and not FINAL.
requirements: Use only the isolated repository and the two inputs listed by TASK.json; preserve inputs and avoid network, MCP, remotes, parent directories, credentials, and historical material.

Design and actually execute a temporal train/validation/test experiment with a naive baseline, predefined metrics, leakage removal, repeated evidence, perturbation tests, deterministic randomness, and retained failures.
Compare structurally distinct feasible candidates with the baseline, run a minimal executable sanity case, and distinguish verified evidence from claims without declaring anything FINAL.
Return exactly one JSON object conforming to observation.schema.json.
robustness_tests: Feature missingness perturbation on every test row left selected persistence MAE/RMSE at 0.814375/1.097692 because the selected rule is feature-independent.
Removing saturated feature row 40 from final training left selected persistence MAE/RMSE at 0.814375/1.097692 because persistence has no fitted training coefficients.
Adding fixed-seed Gaussian feature jitter with standard deviation 0.5 to test features left selected persistence MAE/RMSE at 0.814375/1.097692.

Paired fixed-seed bootstrap of selected-minus-baseline test MAE produced 2.5%, 50%, and 97.5% quantiles all 0 because the selected model and baseline are identical; this supplies reproducibility evidence but no comparative uncertainty evidence.
selected_model: Naive persistence, selected provisionally by lowest unweighted mean MAE over two expanding-window validation folds; this is not a FINAL or deployment decision.
self_reported_limitations: Only local synthetic inputs were used; no external validation or domain references were available or sought.
The regression implementations are deliberately small deterministic candidates, not an exhaustive hyperparameter search.
The selected model is also the baseline, so selected-versus-baseline bootstrap and feature perturbations are necessarily uninformative about comparative superiority.
The first experiment execution failed on the missing lag for row 1; the failure was retained in commands and falsification evidence, then fixed and rerun successfully.
No dependencies or configuration changes were installed or made.

uncertainties: Eight test rows and two validation folds are too few for strong generalization claims, especially after a regime transition.
The field notes do not specify target units, operational loss asymmetry, forecast lead time beyond the assumed one-step task, or acceptable error thresholds.
Invalid calendar labels prevent calendar-aware seasonality, elapsed-time checks, and real-date gap analysis.
The paired bootstrap is conditional on eight observed test rows and does not represent regime-level uncertainty; for selected-versus-baseline it is degenerate because they are the same method.
The robustness perturbations establish feature-independence of persistence, not robustness to target shocks, delayed target availability, or different transition dynamics.
